name: FlexGlue
plain: FlexGlue (ETH Zurich and partners, 2026): sparse matching of two photos of one scene: ALIKED keypoints, DINOv3 ConvNeXt features and a transformer that predicts where each keypoint lands in the other photo; keypoint index pairs. MIT; DINOv3 backbone weights under the DINOv3 licence.
summary: FlexGlue (Lindenberger, Sarlin, Miksik and Pollefeys 2026): sparse feature matching from dense features. ALIKED finds up to 2048 keypoints per image at a 1024-pixel long side, a DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B describes each image at 512 x 512, nine transformer layers (rotary self-attention, cross-attention) relate both feature maps, and a head predicts where each keypoint lands in the other image; mutual nearest neighbours of keypoints and predictions are the matches. Returns both keypoint sets, the index pairs of the matches and their confidence.

papers.title: FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation

licence_notes: The checkpoint includes the DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B backbone weights (`extractor.backbone.*`): the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply) covers them; read it before commercial use.
limitations: Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
No exportable module: the keypoint and match counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
Upstream's sparse mode only: no RoMa v2 refiner, no dense or sampled matches and no covisibility score.
Two resizes per image as upstream: ALIKED sees a long side of `long_side` (aspect kept), the descriptor a `size` x `size` square whatever the aspect ratio.
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead. To reconstruct camera poses from an image folder with these matchers, see [structure from motion](../sfm.md).

variants.name: aliked-flexglue

licence.training_note: FlexGlue: the README states no training data and the training code is not released (see the paper). The DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B backbone was pretrained on LVD-1689M (Meta, not released); ALIKED was trained on MegaDepth.

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls

kernels.protocol: first call, 2 warm-up, peak reset, median of 1 rounds x median of 5
kernels.note: Existing CUDA kernel mode on one fixed input with five warm calls.

tensorrt.part: dense descriptor with eager ALIKED and matching

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, 300 pairs at 768 x 1024, pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. Both modes receive pairs resized to 768 x 1024. Map matched pixels to the calibrated evaluation coordinates and use the same RANSAC seed per pair.

portable32.note: Fixed-size dense descriptor in TensorRT. PyTorch runs ALIKED, the decoder, and sparse matching.

tensorrt.note: Fixed-size dense descriptor in TensorRT. PyTorch runs ALIKED, the decoder, and sparse matching.

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, every 5th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair.

portable32.note: Detector long side 1024 px, up to 2048 keypoints. Same detector setting and 300 calibrated pairs as the original FP32 run.

input.title: Motorcycle, Middlebury 2014 stereo (left and right view, downscaled 4x)

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0052 and p99 <= 0.012 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).
